The manufacturers website shows the correct colors but I didn't go there until after I got my loom. I would also recommend spending $10 more to get the Wonderloom. It helps push the yarn down evenly.

text_fidelity_a:
AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5 This was delivered to my house about an hour ago, and my 6 year old daughter is about to put it away. She's just now finishing up the hardest puzzle included in the kit.

I'm torn on how to review this. It's clearly a nice toy for a lot of kids. The pieces are nice and chunky, the puzzle cards have vibrant artwork, and the app works smoothly. That said, though, there are 12 puzzle cards in the box, and yes, they can be solved multiple ways, but there is no guidance for different combinations of blocks to use to complete the puzzles, so there isn't much incentive to take them off and try again. Also, for someone who is not too far removed from the minimum age range suggested though, it's really easy. Like, a puzzle in two minutes for almost every combo in the deck, except for the boat, which is in the middle of the difficulty spectrum. On the box, with an oddly small top, there are images of three-dimensional shapes made out of the aniblocks, flying around, and the actual blocks do not connect in this way to form them, which was probably the most disappointing part.

The app deserves some special mention. It's certainly good, and easy to use, but it's still an app, and so, of course, it defeats the purpose of having a screen avoidant time to include it. There's also another disadvantage, which is that there are tons of apps that do this same game already, with digital blocks. They offer more puzzles, with more diverse colors of blocks, in more diverse shapes, and a wider variety of difficulty levels.

Overall, I think there are better toys for your money that do very similar things and offer a lot more variety than this. The phone apps, as mentioned before. We have a board game called Blokus 3D (or Rumis) which have a similar pattern-matching idea, but allow for 3D building. There's also Kanoodle Junior, for example, which is excellent, cheaper, ready to travel, and doesn't require an app. 12 puzzles and a handful of two-colored blocks is just not enough for the price. For that reason, I cannot recommend this...but there are far worse options.
text_fidelity_b: AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5

It had really informational highlights about each country, such as eskimos and igloos in Greenland.

This came packaged extremely well. I was very surprised that the edges weren't bent at all after I opened it, and this was because of the high quality packaging. The packaging from T.S. Pros:
+Very solid
+Great world map, that shows Africa as its true size in comparison to the US
+Or in other words, doesn't use the Mercator Projection
+Has very informative information about each country
+You can stick the magnets to your fridge, too
+Extremely excellent packaging
+Very high quality wood backing

Cons:
-The magnets aren't very strong, so you'll be rearranging them a lot

It does have a surprising amount of songs to it. Even several weeks after ownership a few songs were played that we hadn't heard before. But there are some songs that get played all the time. 2 months of ownership and the parents aren't yet annoyed by it so that's a good thing.

I took a star off for the incessant dairy promoting lyrics which just seem strange and I'm convinced that the dairy industry had some involvement in their creation.

text_fidelity_a:
Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set Got this for my toddler - and he loves it! And what little boy wouldn't? It's a very generous set of train toys - so big in fact that it needs to fit in two boxes. The quality of the toys themselves are great - unlike very many toys out there, these feel like they will last for years to come. There's so much variety - but interexchangeability here - that it feels more like legos than anything else - a testament to the creativity of Brio.

The most fascinating thing is that this could be considered a "smart" train set - there is a sensor built into the tunnels so that once the train goes through, it can perform an action like stop, or sound horn. Adds an extra level of interactivity to the set, versus just having it go around in a circle.

The only concern of course is the hefty price tag. It's not cheap, but if you're gearing up for a big birthday bash, this could be the right choice!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set

text_fidelity_a:
Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game Kodama is a game about building massive trees in the forest.

Each turn, players take turns adding branches to their tree that have specific features on them like mushrooms and fireflies on them in an attempt to score points based on the goals of the season (you play through three) and secret goal cards (you choose from four at the beginning of the game). Branch cards can grow outward and upwards, so long as each new card you play touches only one other card you've used thusfar, which is much more difficult than it sounds, and so long as each main branch down to the root can score you ten or less points.

The game itself is OK, but not really very special in any specific way. The artist and producers made the strange choice of making this happy & friendly forest a blend of dark blues, browns and greys that depict a nighttime forest, and it makes the cards a little more difficult to read. It also just looks a little off. Aside from this strange point, the game is not bad, and I like how different it is.
text_fidelity_b: Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game

Melissa & Doug Catch & Count Wooden Fishing Game With 2 Magnetic Rods My boys(1,3, and 5) have all enjoyed this game.

There's several ways to use it. The fish are numbered, so it's great for working on numbers 1-5 for the really little ones. There's also 5 different colors(2 of each). The fish also vary in size, so it's great for size sequencing. The game comes with 2 fishing poles, so your little ones can simply "fish" (there's a magnet on the end of the line, to "catch" the fish) or they can actually play the game using the included spinner.

Since the fishing pole and fish are mostly wood, you can't put these in the water. I have to really push this rule to my boys. They don't understand why they can't put a fishing pole or fish in the water.

The reel DOES wind-up. It doesn't stop, though. You can just keep winding and winding, but the line just rotates out(though the "hook"/line will go up and down in the process).

The only real complaint I have is the red/white floater thing-y. It comes apart, and I'm constantly having to put it back together.

Overall, this is a fun game, and my boys are loving it!

NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 15 Premium Geodes - With Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide, 3 Display Stands, Great STEM Science Toy & Educational Gift I recently received this geode kit. I was eager to bring it to a young friend of mine, a ten year old boy with an eye for science and a curious mind. The package and its photo of a young girl smashing rocks open promises at least a mild adventure, and what young man doesn't enjoy carte blanche to hit things with a hammer?

While my youthful pal did have a good time, I can chalk that more up to a willing sense of adventure than to the kit itself. First, a small gripe. The package depicts a little girl giving the rock her level best with a hammer and wearing safety goggles in the process. No hammer is included, but that's reasonable enough. (If you don't have a hammer, most likely geodes are low on your list of priorities.)

Still, the product seems designed as a dangerous source of fun for latchkey children, as only a single pair of safety goggles are included. Unless NatGeo assumes adults are down with little shards of rock storming their aqua vitreous, they really should have included a second pair. Unlike a hammer, I don't think safety goggles are a household staple.

The bigger issue with the product is the difficulty level in cracking the geodes. A giant Ziploc bag of small-to-medium size rocks is included, as well as some of the trinket-iest "display tables" I've ever seen, pieces of plastic that look to be pilfered from a Playmobil t-ball set. That's beside the point, though. Unless your child is sneaking steroids, these geodes are going to prove a most formidable foe. I cracked and whacked with all my (decent, adult) might and we only managed to get a couple open. If we had kept at it, we surely would have ended up with cartoonishly large dominant arms.

So it is good exercise, and hitting things with a hammer is usually a solid albeit not entirely safe source of fun for a kid. It would be disingenuous to say we had a bad time, but I can't give the product any real recommendation, either. If you do check it out, or get it as a gift, invest in that second pair of safety goggles to avoid giving your eyeballs that hipstery studded look, and don't let any kid hit these rocks by their lonesome if you value their fingers.
text_fidelity_b: NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 15 Premium Geodes - With Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide, 3 Display Stands, Great STEM Science Toy & Educational Gift

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments I used to work in Microbiology and one job in particular pertained to streaking for bacteria and viruses on various types of agar plates. We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!

The box is perfectly sized to fit everything, and I like that it has a list of the planets on the side of the box.

Nature Bound Ant Treehouse Habitat Kit with Sand, Connector Tube, Feeding Stick & Insect Instructions, One Size This ant home(tree house) is much smaller than I was expecting, but it's not tiny. Make sure you look at the measurements, though, so your little ones aren't disappointed.

This comes with great directions, so you're led through what you need to do. You can order ants, but the directions are clear for if you chose to collect your own. The kit comes with a coupon to get cheaper ants. (I can't imagine anyone wanting ants bad enough to pay almost $20 for them.) The coupon and the first order page on the website says you'll get 5-10 ants, but then the main page says 30. Even with the coupon code, you're still paying $9.95 for ants(shipping IS included in that price). I can't pay that much when ants are in such abundance around our home. Again, though, I DO give them credit for the great directions for just using ants from the yard. You aren't expected to buy the ants, but you do have that option. Also, to make it clear, you won't get a queen ant if you order. You'll only get non-reproductive ants. (That information is from the website page for ordering the ants.)

It only took my boys a few minutes to come running with more than enough ants to fill their new little home. Unfortunately, our ants have been very slow to feel at home. One died, though we followed directions exactly. They aren't working together like I thought they would, either. That said, so far it has been greatly exciting to watch what little they have done. One ant looks like Goliath upside the other ants, so he's been easier to watch. It's surprisingly fascinating to watch ants move sand around! I assume there will be more efforts from the other ants with time, but I was expecting quicker results. (I don't blame that on the ant farm, by any means!)

One other complaint is the fact that the bottom goes on so loosely. I kept working with it thinking it should be tighter, but had no luck. This is something that will be best watched without too much handling from children, since there are 4 pieces that are easily removed. This kit comes with a tube, which can connect to another tree house if you chose to buy more. (The 2 side pieces can be removed for this connection.)

Overall, this is a fun kit for kids, but it could have been better designed. Every child needs to have the joy of watching ants work, though! ;)

This bench was the first casualty when it fell apart (into multiple pieces) only a few weeks after purchasing. text_fidelity_a: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack There are 24 different Halloween themed pieces in the box, ranging from pumpkins, to ghosts, to pirate ships, to spiders, to skulls.  The necklaces have a simple snap clasp at the end, and the bracelets have two different size settings.  The lights have three different colors including red, green, and blue.  There are three different setting to the lights with how they flash.  When first turned on, all three of the colors work great.  All the red, green and blue lights work at first.  But after about 10 minutes, the blue light starts to fade, then the green light starts to fade, until only the red light is working.  If turned off and left to sit and rest for a while, then all three light begin to light up and work again, but eventually again only the red light will remain lit.  This happened with all of the necklaces and bracelets in the box.  So as long as the lights are not needed to stay on for long periods of time, they are nice.  If needed for longer periods, two bracelets or necklaces or one of each could be used to alternate between them to give each one a rest by turning it off to refresh the colors.  So if handing these out for Halloween treats, I would recommend giving kids two in order to compensate for the lights not working all the time.
text_fidelity_b: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera After getting an X12 over Christmas, and having an absolute blast crashing into everything while learning to fly indoors, I decided it was time to see what it was like outside. Flying an X12 outside left something to be desired, so I began researching to figure out what might fit the bill. After reading MANY reviews and watching a ton of videos, I chose the X5c. It fit my budget, and I got the impression that it truly was a great quad to learn on.

Well, after only a few short months of owning it I can say with certainty that the X5 has certainly held up its end of the bargain, and then some. I say "X5", and not X5"c", because the camera that comes with this thing is pretty lame. The angle (or field of vision, if you prefer) is very narrow. And I don't know if this is simply an issue with Macs, but I had to reformat the SD-card all the time- simply deleting files didn't work. Otherwise, the camera would believe that there wasn't enough space on the card and wouldn't record. So, this made it very easy for me to make the decision to jettison the camera all together, and just let this bird fly free. And I didn't stop there... the feet were no longer necessary either, so away they went too. The prop guards? Never even bothered attaching them to begin with. Flying this thing was kinda fun before getting rid of that stuff, but it became much more fun without the extra baggage.

From the beginning, I chose to learn on "advanced mode", just because it was faster, more responsive, and more challenging. However, I was by no means "advanced" at flying these things. The first time I took it anyplace that wasn't my tiny front yard, I took it to a local park and flew it up kinda high. Well, then I experienced that common thing where you kinda get disoriented with where the quad is in relation to nearby trees, and somehow I flew it into some woods with it impacting the first few branches at around 50 feet. Somehow, by some miracle, the thing didn't get hung up in any of those branches- I'm attributing that to the fact that it was still winter time (not many leaves to help hold it there)... so, where does it ultimately land? Where else, than in a creek? Yup! Brand new lil quad... in the creek. I just took a big deep breath and hung my head when I realized this. Somehow the thing was still on when I fished it out (it never completely submerged- landed in shallow area). I immediately turned it off and removed the battery before shaking it out best I could. Then I brought it home, opened it up, and placed it on the floor about a foot away from a space heater to allow it to dry out for the rest of the day. The next morning, I put everything back together, popped the recharged battery back in, and everything worked perfectly. From then on, I became much more careful about flying at any sort of altitude that included potential trees... and creeks, for that matter. It also didn't take me long to see the need for more batteries. I bought one of the packages available here on Amazon, where it provides you with four batteries and a 4x1 charger to charge them all simultaneously. I also bought to extra batteries before getting the 4x1. So, now that I have 7 batteries, I find myself not only enjoying the thing more, personally, I also have found more time to teach others how to fly it.

O, and before I forget... another sad, yet awesome, thing that happened: I was on my way to go begin my marathon of marathon study sessions for finals when I stopped by at a nearby church to catch about 10 minutes of flight time. I parked in a different area than usual so that I could see what range I could accomplish, and then flew it back with more altitude and speed than I'd intended.... well, I didn't turn fast enough and right behind me was a nice tree waiting to catch the quad. It got stuck at probably 40 feet up. I found various things laying around to throw at it, and even when I hit it with a lightweight block of wood, the thing still didn't budge. I climbed as high as I could, but the branches became too thin and there was no one around to spot me if I fell. Not worth it. So, I just had to let it be. I thought to myself... o well, you need to study anyway. This thing was obviously only meant to be an ill-fated distraction. So I went on my way and decided that I'd re-evaluate the situation only after I'd gotten through at least half of the material I needed to cover. So, a week and several thunderstorms later, I returned to the scene to find the quad stil sitting up in the tree looking all happy. I devised a telescoping "pushstick" made out of an 8' cardboard tube and some quarter round. I tied a rope to it, climbed the tree as high as I could, and then managed to push the quad out of the tree after extending the "pushstick" to a length of almost 20 feet. Took the quad home, opened it up, and it was bone dry and with no signs of rust of weathering. I put it all back together, and it worked. No problems at all. It's amazing.

I've crashed this thing into everything except for myself or other people. I've let my dog chase it, and eventually she even got ahold of it. Still, the quad survives. It slammed into a road sign at full speed earlier today. It survives. I've put this thing through tons of punishment, and thus far, the only thing I've needed to replace is two of those tiny cogs/gears at the bottom of the motor (the ones that engage with the larger gears that actually spin the props). These smaller gears seem to have a tendency to slip over time, and then they fall off. I've gotten into the habit of performing a little flight check before each flight, and confirming that those are properly seated seems to have made a big difference. Still, I have extras now. In anticipation of eventually burning out a motor, I also went ahead and purchased an extra CW and CCW motor. The nice thing about the prospect of changing out the motors is that the new ones have a metal gear that seems like it won't slip like the little plastic ones do. I dunno; we'll see.

I know I'll eventually destroy this thing, but OMG it blows my mind how much it's been through and is still going strong. I'd post a picture of how beat up it is, but I'm afraid it wouldn't really do it justice. It's scratched all over, one of the props was bent and then reshapaned before getting chewed on by my friend's cat. Still, the quad survives...

Once I finally burn out a motor or somehow destroy this thing, I'll update my review to let you know how it goes. Overall, I'm getting a lot of good times out of it. Still learning new ways to enjoy it. Definitely the start of a new hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera

2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans This is one of the better kits that this brand makes. They're compatible with LEGO, albeit of a lower quality overall, and this is another of their designs that don't come with minifigs, and which isn't inherently designed for them. You'll make model police vehicles, but your LEGO dudes won't go riding around in them - they simply won't fit.

The other big downside is that you don't get to do the bags in order like you do with LEGO. You kind of have to open them all at once and work from one gigantic pile in the center of the table. It's messy and can lead to quitting, but that's all part of the experience.

They will fit somewhat within the tractor component, which is the largest piece of this set, and by far the most interesting. There are a number of playable aspects to this that give you a lot more bang for your buck than the more model-focused kits we've tried from Wishalife previously.

Overall, there's plenty of bricks, OK instructions, a large number of stickers, and plenty of fun to be had here. No, it's not LEGO, but it's not too bad considering. This is a great buy to keep your kids playing for some time.
text_fidelity_b: 2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans

You can wrap it as-is, but you may want to wrap it in tissue paper and place it in another box or gift bag if giving as a gift. You can use the box to store the puzzle pieces, if you wish. . . but. . . you can also use it for other things such as office supplies. .. pencils. . . love letters. . . and so on.
